title: Chicken Riggies
subtitle: Utica rigatoni with chicken, peppers, and a spiced tomato cream sauce
excerpt: A central New York classic: chunks of chicken and sweet or hot peppers in a rich tomato cream sauce tossed with rigatoni. The sauce is bold but not heavy, and it comes together in under an hour.
sourceNotes: Utica, New York Italian-American tradition. Riggies is local shorthand for rigatoni.

recipe.batchNotes: Make a double batch of the sauce and freeze without the cream. Stir in cream and cook pasta fresh when reheating.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: The sauce keeps in the fridge for 2 days. Cook pasta fresh and add cream when reheating.

content.text: Chicken riggies is the dish that put Utica on the food map. The sauce leans on peppers as much as tomato, and the cream is added at the end so it stays bright. Use rigatoni so the sauce gets into the tubes.
Heat the olive oil in the frying pan over a high heat. Season the chicken chunks with salt. Brown them in two batches, 3 minutes per side, then set aside.
If using sausage, add it to the pan and break it up with a spoon. Cook for 4 minutes until browned. Remove and set aside with the chicken.
Lower the heat to medium. Add the onion and peppers to the same pan. Cook for 8 minutes, stirring often, until soft. Add the garlic and chilli flakes and cook for 1 minute more.
Tip in the tomatoes. Return the chicken and sausage to the pan. Stir, cover loosely, and simmer for 15 minutes until the chicken is cooked through.
Cook the rigatoni in a large pan of salted boiling water until just al dente. Reserve a mugful of pasta water, then drain.
Stir the cream into the sauce. Taste and adjust the salt and chilli. Add the rigatoni and toss well, adding a splash of pasta water if the sauce is too thick. Serve with parmesan.

items.symptom: The chicken is dry and stringy.
items.cause: It was overcooked in the browning stage.
items.fix: Brown quickly on high heat to colour only; it will finish cooking in the sauce.

items.cause: The tomatoes were watery or the pan was too wide and sauce evaporated too fast.
items.fix: Simmer uncovered for 5 more minutes before adding the cream. The pasta water thickens it further.

items.cause: The sauce was boiling when the cream went in.
items.fix: Take the pan off the heat or reduce to a low simmer before stirring in the cream.
